analyst.summary: Adani Enterprises is transforming from a trading/incubator conglomerate into an airports-roads-new energy-copper infrastructure platform, and that pivot is real -- about 80% of FY26 operating profit now comes from more mature, contracted businesses. But this year's headline 31% profit growth was almost entirely a one-time gain from exiting the Adani Wilmar edible-oils joint venture, not from the underlying business: the most recent quarter, stripped of that gain, actually posted a loss, hurt by rising depreciation on newly started assets and mining setbacks in Australia. The new growth engines -- airports, the copper smelter, roads, green hydrogen, data centers -- are still ramping up and have already shown delays (the copper plant, in particular, has run well below capacity). At a lofty valuation (a price-to-earnings ratio in the 40s-plus), the market is already pricing in a smooth, multi-year execution of all of these bets simultaneously, funded by continued heavy borrowing. Add a legal overhang that, while easing (the DOJ has moved to drop the US bribery case and settlements are proposed), has not fully cleared, and the risk-reward looks unfavourable at current prices. Recommendation: Sell.
